title: Improving Rural Endometrial Cancer Care
official: Patient Navigation in Gynecologic Oncology: Improving Care Among Marginalized Endometrial Cancer Patients
summary: This is a pilot feasibility study to enable intensive outreach for marginalized patients with endometrial cancer (EC). Rural residents as well as patients who self-identify as Black or African American patients with EC have higher mortality rates. This study aims to introduce a treatment focused patient navigation intervention for marginalized patients with EC to address the multiple barriers these patients face. Patient navigation is a personalized program to help patients navigate the health care system and access medical and non-medical services. For example, patient navigators can provide services such as mediating/facilitating communication between patients and their providers/health care team, advocating for patient needs, identifying financial assistance and insurance-related resources, coordinating complex patient care, and providing patients with psychosocial support. This study will assess the implementation and effectiveness of a navigation intervention targeting multilevel barriers to care. The primary objective is to evaluate the fidelity of following the patient navigation intervention protocol.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Written informed consent obtained to participate in the study and HIPAA authorization for release of personal health information. Subject is willing and able to comply with study procedures.
* Age ≥ 18 years at the time of consent.
* Resides in a \>25 miles between a patient's home and University of North Carolina Hospital
* patients who self-identify as Black or African American race
* Newly diagnosed or recurrent diagnosis of endometrial cancer undergoing treatment planning at University of North Carolina

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients who are not receiving treatment within the UNC health care system
* Non-English-speaking patients
